row.title: git memory duplicate commit records from unnormalized repo urls
row.summary: git memory tools can create duplicate commit provenance records for the same hash when repo urls use different formats.
row.content: bug report from user: memory git provenance records may duplicate the same commit because repo identifiers are stored/searched in different formats, for example `github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app` versus `git@github.com:j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app.git`. this causes `memory_release_candidates_search` to return multiple candidates for the same commit hash, and `memory_release_notes_preview` can show both normal release bullets and a needs-context entry for the same commit. recommended fix: normalize repo urls before storing and searching so `git@github.com:j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app.git`, `https://github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app.git`, and `github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app` converge to `github.com/j0k3r-dev-rgl/sias-app`; dedupe by `normalized_repo + commit_hash`; apply the same dedupe in release notes preview.

row.title: repo url normalization bug confirmed in git memory code
row.summary: read-only investigation confirmed git memory commit records only lowercase/trim repo strings, so different url formats are not canonicalized or deduped.
row.content: investigation result: the duplicate commit candidate bug is code-related. in `extensions/memory/src/commit-changelog.ts`, repo handling uses `normalizetext`, which only trims and lowercases strings. `buildcommitmetadata`, `buildcommitpayload`, `addcommitrecord`, `findactiveduplicatecommit`, and `passesstructuredfilters` compare/store raw normalized text, so `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`, and `github.com/owner/repo` remain distinct. `searchreleasecandidates` returns all matching active commit records without deduping by repo/hash, and `previewreleasenotes` iterates those candidates directly, so duplicate records can appear as both release bullets and needs-context. existing tests only cover exact same repo-string dedupe and current head storage preserving the full https remote url; they do not cover cross-format repo canonicalization for commit records. `parsegitremote` in `context.ts` already canonicalizes project ids for git remotes but is not used by commit/changelog provenance code.

row.title: fixed git memory repo url dedupe bug
row.summary: implemented canonical repo url normalization and dedupe for git memory commit records, release candidates, and release notes preview.
row.content: progress: fixed the git memory duplicate commit bug in `extensions/memory/src/commit-changelog.ts`. repo identifiers are now canonicalized for commit storage/search/dedupe so ssh, https, and host/path github formats converge to `github.com/owner/repo`. duplicate commit add detection now compares normalized repo + commit_hash. release candidate search dedupes legacy duplicate records by normalized repo + commit_hash, prefers records with richer changelog/release context, and suppresses all duplicate identities once any equivalent commit record is linked to a release/changelog release. tests were added/updated in `extensions/memory/test/memory.test.ts` for cross-format add dedupe, current head canonical repo storage, release candidate/preview dedupe, needs-context suppression, and post-release suppression. validation passed: targeted vitest cases, `cd extensions/memory && npm test` (95 tests), `cd extensions/memory && npm run typecheck`, and `git diff --check`.

row.title: sdd implementation map artifact policy

row.content: decision/progress: the sdd workflow was updated to introduce `openspec/changes/<change>/implementation-map.md` as a separate operational handoff artifact for formal openspec/hybrid sdd flows. the map is for explored files, relevant symbols, expected files to modify/create/delete, behavioral findings, constraints/risks, validation commands, open questions, and downstream handoff notes. it is explicitly separate from `metadata.yaml` and non-normative relative to metadata, approved prd, spec, design, and tasks. updated `skills/sdd-workflow/skill.md` plus sdd phase subagents (`sdd-explore`, `sdd-proposal`, `sdd-spec`, `sdd-design`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-apply`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-archive`) so phases read/update/preserve the implementation map according to their responsibilities. validation: `skill_registry_generate` reported 11 skills and unchanged generated artifacts; `skill_registry_resolve` routed sdd implementation-map paths to `sdd-workflow`; `git diff --check` passed. prd workflow was intentionally left for a separate future discussion.

row.title: prd workflow review findings
row.summary: read-only review found prd flow is conceptually sound but lacks a canonical prd template and explicit approval/readiness handoff semantics.
row.content: read-only review of prd flow: `sdd-workflow` currently makes prd optional, orchestrator-authored, and reviewed by `prd-review` when readiness is uncertain. `prd-review` checks ambiguity, contradictions, testability gaps, metadata alignment, security/privacy risks, and readiness for downstream sdd. strengths: prd drafting stays with orchestrator/user context; review is separate; critical debts block implementation; downstream sdd phases treat approved prd as context and must flag conflicts. gaps: no canonical prd template in `sdd-workflow`; no explicit prd status marker/approval handoff beyond conversation/orchestrator decision; prd review does not produce a structured requirement/acceptance-criteria coverage matrix for downstream spec; downstream phases read prd only when supplied/requested, which can allow prd context to be dropped; prd vs proposal responsibilities overlap and may duplicate product-level content; no explicit rule that prd must avoid implementation/file-level details now covered by `implementation-map.md`. potential future change: add a prd template and lifecycle states, require approved prd context handoff when a prd exists and is in-scope, clarify prd/proposal boundary, and ensure prd review outputs structured acceptance criteria/questions for sdd.

row.title: youtube transcript repair research findings
row.summary: community evidence and code inspection indicate youtube transcript failures should be handled by staged fallback and clear diagnostics rather than assuming captions are permanently disabled.
row.content:
type: learning
context: youtube-research extension repair investigation
findings: the extension uses yt-dlp for youtube transcript sources and fetches. community reports in yt-dlp/yt-dlp#13831 and youtube-transcript-api#303 show that youtube often returns transcript/subtitle failures because of ip/cloud blocking, anti-bot fingerprinting, translated/automatic subtitle rate limits, or 429s, even when captions exist in browser. yt-dlp maintainers recommend considering current/nightly yt-dlp, curl_cffi/impersonation where applicable, and handling subtitle fetch failures gracefully; comments also note json3 retries may sometimes work better than vtt.
code implication: extensions/youtube-research currently builds a transcript plan, but runtranscriptget selects one candidate and if client.fetchtranscript fails or returns empty, it fails without trying remaining best-effort candidates or metadata fallback. restrictive modes can remain strict, but auto/best-effort should likely iterate candidates, collect failed attempts, and fallback to description/chapters/metadata with clear diagnostics.

row.content: created a new global pi extension at ~/.pi/agent/extensions/code-research/ (previously named find-symbol) that registers a custom tool 'find_symbol'. it uses native tree-sitter bindings (tree-sitter 0.21.1, tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2, tree-sitter-javascript 0.23.1, tree-sitter-java 0.23.5, minimatch 10.2.5) to parse ts/js/java files and return structured symbol locations. architecture is modular: index.ts registers the tool, src/core/parser.ts caches parsers, src/core/resolver.ts orchestrates search with per-call parse cache and pluggable language adapters, src/languages/typescript.ts extracts symbols for ts/js, src/languages/java.ts extracts symbols for java. supports parameters path, symbol, language (ts/js/java/auto), kind, include_signature, include_code, scope, glob, and search_mode (exact/prefix/contains). include_code is restricted to function/method kinds and disabled for non-exact searches. finds private members including hash-private (#name) in ts and private fields/methods in java. handles abstract classes, type aliases, nested functions, constructors, getters, setters, static methods. interface implementation detection works syntactically via implements clause for ts and java. includes example fixtures in examples/typescript/, examples/javascript/, and examples/java/. tested with the spring project at ~/sias/app/back. tests run with vitest and pass.

row.title: typescript tools derive project roots from nearest markers with source-root fallback
row.summary: ts/js code-research tools can reuse a shared project-root resolver that prefers nearest package or ts/js config markers and falls back to parent of app/src when markers are absent
row.content:
type: architecture
context: fixing ts/js function_call_tree for absolute file paths outside pi cwd.
decision: shared ts/js root resolution now lives in languages/typescript/shared.ts as resolvetypescriptprojectroot(targetpath, isdirectory). it searches upward from the target for the nearest project markers (package.json, tsconfig.json, jsconfig.json, bun/package/pnpm/yarn lockfiles, deno config). if none are found, it falls back to the parent of source roots like app or src, then finally to the target directory.
implication: future ts/js tools can index from a stable project root even when invoked on an absolute file path from outside the target repo. this specifically avoids accidental indexing from pi cwd and should be reused by the next ts/js tool that needs project-level indexing.

row.title: ts function-call-tree robust root resolution now indexes build artifacts and hits parser size limit
row.summary: after switching ts/js function_call_tree to project-root indexing, real projects with build outputs can fail with invalid argument because the index walks build files larger than the shared 1mb tree-sitter buffer
row.content:
type: bug
context: validating function_call_tree against /home/j0k3r/sias/app/front after adding robust ts/js project-root detection.
evidence: function_call_tree on real ts files now returns invalid argument instead of not_found. the derived project root is correct, but collectsupportedfiles in src/languages/typescript/function-call-tree.ts recursively indexes everything except node_modules and dot directories, so it includes build/server/index.js. that file is 1342276 bytes in sias front. parsing it directly with the extension's javascript parser and buffersize 1048576 reproduces the exact error: invalid argument.

implication: fixing ts/js root resolution exposed a second issue. future remediation can either narrow indexed directories/files for ts/js source analysis, skip parse-failing files during directory indexing like find_symbol does, increase or dynamically size the parser buffer, or combine these approaches.

row.title: ts js function-call-tree should index application source not generated outputs
row.summary: for ts/js call trees the tool should be source-oriented and skip generated/framework output directories and parse-failing files instead of aborting the whole analysis
row.content:
type: decision
context: refining the purpose of function_call_tree after comparing the successful java output with failing ts/js behavior on a real react router project.
decision: ts/js function_call_tree indexes application code only. generated outputs and framework caches are excluded from recursive indexing (node_modules, build, dist, coverage, .next, .nuxt, .svelte-kit, .react-router, .turbo, .vite, .cache, out). if a remaining file still fails to parse, indexing skips that file rather than failing the whole call-tree request.
rationale: the tool is meant to give the agent a fast whole-function application call tree for debugging and understanding behavior, not to traverse compiled bundles or generated framework artifacts.
